description:
Reports say some teams in The Hundred linked to IPL ownership may avoid signing Pakistani players at the next auction.
The issue has raised concerns about possible discrimination and unequal opportunities in franchise cricket.
Azeem Rafiq, former Yorkshire player and anti-discrimination advocate, told Al Jazeera the trend is worrying but not new.
He said Pakistani players have long been sidelined from leagues connected to the Indian Premier League.
Rafiq criticised the England and Wales Cricket Board, saying it chose money over inclusion when selling teams.
He argued there is little the ECB can now do to stop franchises acting as they wish.
He added that exclusion leaves Pakistani players disadvantaged financially, professionally and in global exposure.

description:
The Oscar-nominated film 'The Voice of Hind Rajab' was among the nominees at this year's BAFTA Film Awards in London. 
The documentary tells the story of five-year-old Hind Rajab, a Palestinian girl killed by Israeli forces in Gaza whilst calling for help, using her real voice from the emergency call recording. 
Hind's mother, Wesam Hamada, attended the ceremony and said the film gives dignity to her daughter and conveys the voices of all children in Gaza to the world. 
The film has attracted support from executive producers including Brad Pitt and Alfonso Cuaron.

Al Jazeera's Milena Veselinovic reports from London.

The Mexican army has killed a drug boss who led one of the country's most powerful criminal organisations.
Nemesio Oseguera, or "El Mencho," was the head of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.
The gang is known for trafficking drugs into the US, which had put a $15-million bounty on El Mencho's arrest. 
His killing has triggered a wave of violence in several areas. 
The ⁠Mexican Embassy in Washington says US intelligence contributed to the operation that led to his death.

Al Jazeera’s John Holman reports from Mexico City.

⁠Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says talks with the US on Iran's nuclear programme have been encouraging - ahead of another round of indirect negotiations set for Thursday in Geneva.
It follows threats of limited strikes by US President Donald Trump, to force Tehran to reach a deal.
“Iran is committed to peace and stability in the region,” Pezeshkian wrote on X.
“Recent negotiations involved the exchange of practical proposals and yielded encouraging signals. However, we continue to closely monitor US actions and have made all necessary preparations for any potential scenario,” he said.
The US President's Special Envoy Steve Witkoff will take part in Thursday's talks in Geneva. 
He says President Trump thought Iran would have buckled to the military pressure by now.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Pakistan says it has killed at least 80 fighters from the Pakistani Taliban in air strikes targeting armed groups in Afghanistan's Nangarhar and Paktika provinces. 
Afghan authorities dispute the claim, saying the bombardment hit a religious school and homes, killing many civilians including women and children. 
Witnesses describe multiple strikes beginning at midnight. One survivor lost 15 family members, most of them children. 
The escalation threatens to further destabilise already fragile relations between the two neighbours, following failed diplomatic talks and border confrontations last year.

Al Jazeera's Kamal Hyder reports from Peshawar, Pakistan.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A Palestinian boy has died after waiting 14 months for Israeli authorities to allow his medical evacuation from Gaza, despite having approved papers. 
Nidal Abu Rabeea suffered from organ failure and required urgent treatment abroad, but Israel blocked his departure even after granting rare permission. 
Under the ceasefire agreement, Israel pledged to allow 50 critically ill patients to leave daily through the Rafah crossing, but only a handful have been permitted to exit since October. 
Nidal's mother is calling on Israel, international organisations and human rights groups to prevent further deaths caused by the restrictions on medical evacuations.

Al Jazeera's Hani Mahmoud reports from Gaza City, Palestine.
